structured_output.hypothesis: If W = kL³ and the value of k changes with body length during growth, then in a large sample of measured individuals, Fulton's K (= 100·W/L³) will vary systematically with length, and the log-log slope of weight on length will differ from 3. Species with a slope near 3 will show constant K.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Use North Sea IBTS Q1 and Q3 individual fish records (length and individual weight) for species with at least 500 weighed fish spanning at least a 3-fold range of length. Fit log W = a + b·log L for each species. (i) Constancy arm: among species whose 95% CI for b includes 3 (|b−3| ≤ 0.1), the Spearman correlation of K with length class is |rho| < 0.2 and the K change between the smallest and largest length quartiles is < 10%. (ii) Change arm: among species whose 95% CI for b excludes 3 by more than 0.1, K differs by ≥ 10% between the smallest and largest length quartiles, with the sign of the K trend matching the sign of b−3. (iii) Prevalence: at least 50% of eligible species show b significantly different from 3 (|b−3| > 0.1), which supports the claim that form change is likely while growth continues. The claim passes only if all three conditions hold.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim fails if any of these occurs. (a) Fewer than 50% of eligible species have |b−3| > 0.1 with the 95% CI excluding 3. (b) K varies by ≥ 10% across length quartiles in species whose b is statistically indistinguishable from 3 (|b−3| ≤ 0.1), which would mean K does not track the allometric slope. (c) K is flat (change < 10% across length quartiles) in species with b clearly different from 3.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'k' is the weight-length coefficient, with density assumed constant. It maps to Fulton's condition factor K = 100·W/L³, using DATRAS individual weight (IndWgt, g) and total length (LngtClass, with the LngtCode unit). 'Alteration in general form' maps to allometric growth: a length-weight exponent b ≠ 3, so that K changes with length. Modern reinterpretation: K also reflects condition, fat reserves, gonad state, season and stomach contents, not form alone. The plan therefore analyses within-species and within-survey-quarter strata and ignores sex and maturity effects beyond stratification. Density is assumed constant, as in Thompson's premise. 'Likely as long as growth continues' is operationalised as the share of species with b significantly different from 3.

dataset.name: DATRAS (Database of Trawl Surveys), ICES
dataset.publisher: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES)
dataset.why_it_fits: DATRAS offers free raw-data download and web services, and also has the icesDATRAS R package on CRAN. The fetched landing page does not itself list the biological records. I am relying on the DATRAS exchange format, whose CA (age/length) records include length class, individual weight, species (Valid_Aphia) and sex, and I have not verified this on the page. The planned fields are LngtClass, LngtCode, IndWgt, Valid_Aphia, Quarter, Survey and Year. Because the records are measured and cover many species and size ranges, they can test K against length for each species.
